A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Agile Deliberation. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison; v1 Appendices A–D correspond to v2 Appendices C, E, F, and G.

before.justification: v1 reports original expert interviews, analysis of expert-authored definitions, and an 18-session user study, including classification results, survey statistics, and qualitative findings.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds classification results testing definition transfer to two Qwen VLMs in Appendix B and Table 3.

M1.justification: The concept decomposition, borderline retrieval, ambiguity clustering, and feedback-based refinement procedures remain unchanged, including the prompts and system parameters. The Qwen experiment applies existing definitions to other classifiers without revising the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use paid to play and healthy food, the proprietary 100M-image collection and WebLI, and the same user study. v2 clarifies that participants lacked professional moderation experience; it does not report a changed population. The transfer experiment retains the existing tasks.

E2.justification: The original comparison retains Zero-shot, Modeling Collaborator, and Manual Deliberation. Table 1's new 'Assigned Deliberation System' label clarifies existing Agile and Manual scores. The transfer experiment uses existing comparator methods with different VLM backbones.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds a classification-only transfer protocol: definitions produced using Gemini 2.5 Flash are applied to Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct. The original study design, session budgets, 200-image test sets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new transfer experiment tests whether existing definitions remain useful across models and how their benefits depend on model capability. This is a targeted portability analysis; v2 explicitly acknowledges that component ablations and full-pipeline evaluation across models remain unperformed.

E5.justification: Both versions report participant means and standard deviations and retain the same survey significance reporting. Table 3 follows the existing mean-and-standard-deviation practice. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 retain their original results. New Table 3 reports Agile-condition F1 scores of 0.52 and 0.52 for paid to play and healthy food on Qwen3-VL-8B, and 0.59 and 0.52 on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct, alongside zero-shot and Manual-condition results. These are additional backbone-specific outcomes, not revisions to the original scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(12), optimization rules, and adaptive DBSCAN algorithm are retained. Algorithm relocation and differences in PDF equation text encoding do not change their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the two-stage framework and claims of improved classification, clearer concept understanding, and reduced user effort. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands the qualifications concerning statistical power and generalizability, absent component ablations, and reliance on one model for the full pipeline. Appendix B adds the interpretation that Agile definitions are richer and more sensitive to model capability. v1 discussed study constraints but lacked this broader limitations account and transfer interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, documents the study interface through Figures 4–7, and specifies participants' lack of professional moderation experience. Existing prompts, retrieval parameters, clustering settings, and refinement-candidate counts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds five cited works covering Policy Maps, Promptimizer, Qwen3, and two studies of human/model uncertainty. These support study-scale context, transfer evaluation, and the existing uncertainty motivation. The main research positioning remains stable; publication and title updates to existing references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section organization are preserved. v2 adds acknowledgements and appendix sections on limitations, transferability, and the interface, renumbers retained appendices, updates author affiliations, and makes localized wording corrections.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands visual documentation with Table 3 and Figures 4–7, showing concept selection, editable definitions, image labeling and feedback, and the refined definition. Table 1 also receives clearer row labels and an explanatory caption. Original Figures 1–3 are retained, while Algorithm 1 is relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful portability evidence, explicit limitations, a code-access reference, and concrete interface documentation, while correcting Table 1's ambiguous attribution of Manual-condition scores. These improve transparency and interpretability. The gains remain limited: the user-study scale and missing ablations are unchanged, and transferring fixed definitions does not establish full-pipeline generalization or the proposed explanation involving richer definitions.
